result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly identify proportional figures as the cause and give a pasteable tabular-nums fix that keeps Gill Sans. B is stronger: it keeps right alignment in the fix, adds lining-nums to handle old-style figures, and honestly says CSS cannot fake tabular figures when the font lacks them. A's fallback, a min-width inline-block span, would not actually align digits of different widths, and its DevTools check confirms the property is set rather than that the font supports it, a flaw B shares. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly identify proportional figures as the cause and keep Gill Sans. B's fallback is wrong: a fixed-width inline-block span with min-width in ch only pads the whole number, so the digits inside are still proportional and won't line up. A is right that CSS can't fake tabular figures. A's DevTools check is weak because the Computed panel shows the declared value, not whether the font supports tnum, but that is a smaller flaw than B's.
